root_cause.text: The option parsing loops in `xt_tcpudp` and `xt_dccp` lack boundary checks before accessing `op[i+1]` to determine option length, allowing an out-of-bounds read when the final buffer byte indicates a multi-byte option.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `|| i == optlen - 1` to the conditional guarding the `op[i + 1]` dereference in `tcp_find_option` and `dccp_find_option`, preventing access past the end of the option area as described in the CVE.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement accesses op[i + 1] to determine option length without validating that i + 1 + op[i + 1] stays within buffer bounds. When the final buffer byte indicates a multi-byte option extending past the buffer, this causes an out-of-bounds read.

This statement accesses op[i + 1] on line 65 without sufficient boundary validation. Similar to xt_dccp.c, it lacks checks ensuring i + 1 + op[i + 1] remains within buffer bounds, enabling out-of-bounds read when crafted options specify lengths extending past the buffer.
